title: Hilbert--Samuel polynomial has degree equal to local Krull dimension
statement: Let $(R,\mathfrak n)$ be a nonzero Noetherian local commutative ring [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring]. There exist a nonzero polynomial $Q_R(X)\in\mathbf Q[X]$ and an integer $N\ge1$ such that, for every integer $n\ge N$, the module $R/\mathfrak n^n$ has finite composition length [def-weil-pbc-module-length] and $\mathrm{length}_R(R/\mathfrak n^n)=Q_R(n)$. The leading coefficient of $Q_R$ is strictly positive, and its degree equals $\dim R$, the Krull dimension [def-weil-pbc-krull-dimension-ring].

source.place: Tag 00K8, proposition-hilbert-function-polynomial, applied to M=R and I=n, together with Tag 00KQ, proposition-dimension, equivalence (1) <=> (2); shifting chi(n)=length(R/n^(n+1)) to n does not change its degree.

proof.text: Put $\mathfrak m=\mathfrak n$, $k=R/\mathfrak m$ and $H_R(n)=\mathrm{length}_R(R/\mathfrak m^n)$ for $n\ge1$, with $H_R(0)=0$. By [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], choose generators $y_1,\ldots,y_t$ of $\mathfrak m$. The degree-$i$ monomials in the $y_j$ span $\mathfrak m^i/\mathfrak m^{i+1}$ over $k$, so these spaces are finite-dimensional. An $R$-submodule of a module killed by $\mathfrak m$ is exactly a $k$-subspace; a basis flag therefore has composition factors $k$, of length one. Thus these pieces have $R$-length equal to their $k$-dimension. The filtration by powers of $\mathfrak m$ and [lem-weil-pbc-length-additive-short-exact] now give, for every $n\ge1$, finiteness and the identity $H_R(n)=\sum_{i=0}^{n-1}\dim_k(\mathfrak m^i/\mathfrak m^{i+1})$.

source.place: Tag 00K8, proposition-hilbert-function-polynomial, and the preceding paragraph defining phi and chi; finite-length filtration written out.

proof.text: Form $S=\bigoplus_{i\ge0}\mathfrak m^i/\mathfrak m^{i+1}$, with product $[a]_i[b]_j=[ab]_{i+j}$. Changing a representative changes the product by an element of $\mathfrak m^{i+j+1}$, so it is well defined. Its degree zero is $k$, and the degree-one classes of the $y_j$ generate it, by the monomial description in step 1. Thus $S$ is standard graded in [def-pc-standard-graded-algebra]. Apply [lem-trf-standard-graded-hilbert-function] with $M=S$ (generated by its unit in degree zero). We obtain $P\in\mathbf Q[X]$ such that $\dim_k(\mathfrak m^i/\mathfrak m^{i+1})=P(i)$ for all sufficiently large $i$.

source.place: Tag 00K8, proposition-hilbert-function-polynomial, proof: associated graded ring; Tag 00K1.

proof.text: The polynomials $\binom{X}{j}$ form a rational basis, since their degrees are $j$ with nonzero leading coefficients $1/j!$. Write $P(X)=\sum_j a_j\binom{X}{j}$. The identity $\binom{i+1}{j+1}-\binom{i}{j+1}=\binom{i}{j}$ shows by telescoping that the tail sum in step 1 equals $\sum_j a_j\binom{n}{j+1}$ plus a rational constant accounting for the initial terms. Hence $H_R(n)=Q_R(n)$ eventually for some $Q_R\in\mathbf Q[X]$. Since $\mathfrak m^n\subseteq\mathfrak m\ne R$, every $R/\mathfrak m^n$ is nonzero and $H_R(n)\ge1$. Therefore $Q_R\ne0$; its leading coefficient is positive, because a nonzero rational polynomial has the sign of its leading coefficient at sufficiently large positive integers. Write $e_R=\deg Q_R\ge0$. These three steps apply to every nonzero Noetherian local ring.

For the upper bound let $d=\dim R$. By [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-local-system-of-parameters], $d$ is finite and there is $J=(x_1,\ldots,x_d)\subseteq\mathfrak m$ with $\mathfrak m^a\subseteq J$ for some $a\ge1$. Hence $R/J$ is a quotient of the finite-length module $R/\mathfrak m^a$; let its length be $L$. For $d\ge1$, the degree-$i$ monomials in the $x_j$ give a surjection from $\binom{i+d-1}{d-1}$ copies of $R/J$ onto $J^i/J^{i+1}$. Length additivity [lem-weil-pbc-length-additive-short-exact], first for the kernel of this surjection and then for the $J$-power filtration, gives $\mathrm{length}_R(R/J^n)\le L\sum_{i=0}^{n-1}\binom{i+d-1}{d-1}=L\binom{n+d-1}{d}$. Since $J^n\subseteq\mathfrak m^n$, the quotient $R/J^n\twoheadrightarrow R/\mathfrak m^n$ bounds $H_R(n)$ by this same degree-$d$ polynomial. If $d=0$, the cited statement gives $J=0$ and $\mathfrak m^a=0$, so $H_R(n)=\mathrm{length}_R(R)$ for $n\ge a$. In either case the positive leading coefficient from step 3 forces $e_R\le d$.

source.place: Tag 00KQ, proposition-dimension, proof of d-prime(R) >= d(R), with the d=0 case kept separately.

proof.text: To obtain the opposite bound, let $(A,\mathfrak a)$ be any Noetherian local domain and $0\ne x\in\mathfrak a$. Put $B=A/(x)$, a nonzero Noetherian local ring. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-artin-rees] to $M=A$, $N=xA$ and $I=\mathfrak a$, enlarging its constant to $c\ge1$. For $n>c$, $xA\cap\mathfrak a^n\subseteq\mathfrak a^{n-c}xA$. The exact quotient sequence and [lem-weil-pbc-length-additive-short-exact] give $H_B(n)=H_A(n)-\mathrm{length}_A(xA/(xA\cap\mathfrak a^n))\le H_A(n)-H_A(n-c)$. Here multiplication by $x$ identifies $A$ with $xA$, so $xA/\mathfrak a^{n-c}xA\cong A/\mathfrak a^{n-c}$; the indicated inclusion gives the needed surjection onto this quotient. Also $B/\mathfrak a^nB=A/(xA+\mathfrak a^n)$, and its $A$- and $B$-submodules coincide, so its two lengths agree. Step 3 supplies the polynomials for $A$ and $B$. Since $H_B(n)\ge1$, $e_A=0$ is impossible: then $Q_A(n)-Q_A(n-c)=0$. For $e_A\ge1$, that difference has degree $e_A-1$ and positive leading coefficient $c e_A\operatorname{lc}(Q_A)$. Comparing eventual values yields $e_B\le e_A-1$.

source.place: Tag 00KQ, proposition-dimension, prime-chain argument using Tag 00KC; the needed estimate is derived directly from Tag 00IN, lemma-Artin-Rees, instead of importing the Hilbert exact-sequence lemmas.

proof.text: Prove by strong induction on $e_R$ that every chain of prime ideals of $R$ has length at most $e_R$. Chains of length zero already satisfy this. Given a strict chain $\mathfrak p_0\subsetneq\mathfrak p_1\subsetneq\cdots\subsetneq\mathfrak p_l$ with $l\ge1$, put $A=R/\mathfrak p_0$ and choose $x\in\mathfrak p_1/\mathfrak p_0$, $x\ne0$. All these primes lie in the maximal ideal of the local ring, so $x$ is in the maximal ideal of $A$. Quotient ideals correspond to ideals containing the kernel, showing directly that $A$, and $B=A/(x)$, are nonzero Noetherian local rings; $A$ is a domain since $\mathfrak p_0$ is prime. The surjections $R/\mathfrak m^n\twoheadrightarrow A/(\mathfrak mA)^n$ and length additivity [lem-weil-pbc-length-additive-short-exact] give $e_A\le e_R$ (lengths over the quotient ring agree by their identical submodule lattices). Step 5 implies $e_A\ge1$ and $e_B<e_R$. Thus if $e_R=0$ such a chain is impossible, which proves the base case. Otherwise the induction hypothesis applies to $B$. Its distinct primes $\mathfrak p_1/(\mathfrak p_0,x)\subsetneq\cdots\subsetneq\mathfrak p_l/(\mathfrak p_0,x)$ form a chain of length $l-1$, so $l-1\le e_B\le e_A-1\le e_R-1$. Therefore $l\le e_R$. Taking the supremum in [def-weil-pbc-krull-dimension-ring] gives $\dim R\le e_R$.

source.place: Tag 00KQ, proposition-dimension, last prime-chain paragraph; strong induction and the degree-zero case made explicit.

proof.text: Steps 4 and 6 give $\deg Q_R=e_R=\dim R$. Step 3 gives $Q_R\ne0$ and its positive leading coefficient. Choose $N\ge1$ larger than the threshold in step 3. Step 1 gives finite composition length for every $n\ge1$, and step 3 gives $\mathrm{length}_R(R/\mathfrak n^n)=Q_R(n)$ for $n\ge N$, with exactly the exponent in the statement.

source.place: Tags 00K8 and 00KQ; conclusion with exponent n rather than n+1.

lean.statement: theorem exists_hilbertSamuel_polynomial (R : Type u) [CommRing R] [IsNoetherianRing R] [IsLocalRing R] : ∃ Q : Polynomial ℚ, Q ≠ 0 ∧ 0 < Q.leadingCoeff ∧ (Q.natDegree : WithBot ℕ∞) = ringKrullDim R ∧ ∃ N : ℕ, 1 ≤ N ∧ ∀ n : ℕ, N ≤ n → Module.length R (R ⧸ (maximalIdeal R) ^ n) < ⊤ ∧ ((Module.length R (R ⧸ (maximalIdeal R) ^ n)).toNat : ℚ) = Q.eval (n : ℚ)
